evidence.note: Early explicit ordered plan: list checkpoints, evaluate base model to confirm baseline, find correct renderer, evaluate existing checkpoints, then train if <45% — a clear multi-milestone campaign with the 45% target as terminal check.

Cheap end-to-end pass FIRST: tested the custom eval script on limit=5, then a checkpoint on limit=5, then scaled to 100/200 before committing to full 541-sample runs — validating the harness on a tiny run before expensive evaluation.

Progressive sample-size scaling with numeric done-checks: 20→200→541 samples, with a stated rule 'if ≥44% on 50, do full 541 eval', and full-eval confirmations (40.85%, 43.62%, 44.92%) as stage success criteria.

Milestones sequenced by risk/information value: fixed SDK blocker, then tokenizer blocker (unsloth substitute), then evaluated banked existing checkpoints, then launched Tulu3 training as a hedge; wrote best-so-far artifact to best_checkpoint.txt as a checkpoint of verified progress.

Terminal gate reached and verified on full 541 samples (45.66%), structure was revised as results arrived rather than following one open-ended run; but own training runs (v1 enum, v2/v3 stuck) never completed and lacked a clean go/no-go, and structure stayed prose-based (no maintained checklist).

reasoning: The agent went well beyond the level-5 'train then eval' pattern: it validated the eval harness on a tiny limit=5 run before scaling, sequenced milestones by risk (SDK and tokenizer blockers first, then banked existing checkpoints, then training as a hedge), attached concrete numeric/artifact success criteria to each stage (progressive sample sizes, the ≥44%→full-eval rule, best_checkpoint.txt writes), and revised its plan as scores came in — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because time-budget sizing was loose, per-stage go/no-go thresholds were informal, and the structure lived in repeated prose plans rather than a maintained living milestone list.
